controls.title: Centralized logging
controls.objective: Security logs from critical systems are collected centrally and retained for a defined period.

evidence.description: Log source list and retention settings

questions.text: Days of security log retention in the central log platform
questions.guidance: Check retention settings and the oldest available event.

questions.text: Percentage of critical systems sending logs to the central platform
questions.guidance: Compare the log source list with the critical system inventory.

references.source: NIST CSWP 29, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
references.note: wording to be checked against CSWP 29

controls.title: Security alert monitoring
controls.objective: Security alerts are monitored around the clock and triaged within defined times.

evidence.description: SOC or MDR contract and SLA

questions.text: Are security alerts monitored 24 hours a day, by in-house staff or a managed provider?
Median time from a high-severity alert to analyst triage over the last 30 days

references.source: NIST CSWP 29, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
references.note: wording to be checked against CSWP 29

controls.title: Endpoint detection and response
controls.objective: Endpoints and servers run EDR that reports to monitored tooling.

questions.text: Percentage of endpoints and servers with an active, reporting EDR agent
questions.guidance: Compare EDR console count with the hardware inventory.

references.source: NIST CSWP 29, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
references.note: wording to be checked against CSWP 29

controls.title: Physical and cyber event correlation
controls.objective: Physical security events (access denials, door forced, camera loss) reach the team that analyzes cyber events.

evidence.description: Integration between access control or video and the SIEM

questions.text: Are access control and video system events (door forced, repeated denials, camera offline) forwarded to the SIEM or reviewed by the security operations team?
questions.guidance: Partial: reviewed manually but not integrated.

references.source: NIST CSWP 29, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
references.note: wording to be checked against CSWP 29

controls.title: Incident declaration criteria
controls.objective: Criteria for declaring an incident are defined and applied.

questions.text: Are there written criteria for when an adverse event is declared an incident, including severity levels?

references.source: NIST CSWP 29, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
